Please provide an MRP to make this easier to test and fix:
- A small Godot project which reproduces the issue, with no unnecessary files included. Be sure to not include the `.godot` folder in the archive (but keep `project.godot`).
- Having an MRP is very important for contributors to be able to reproduce the bug in the same way that you are experiencing it. When testing a potential fix for the issue, contributors will use the MRP to validate that the fix is working as intended.
- Drag and drop a ZIP archive to upload it (max 10 MB). **Do not select another field until the project is done uploading.**
- **Note for C# users:** If your issue is *not* C#-specific, please upload a minimal reproduction project written in GDScript. This will make it easier for contributors to reproduce the issue locally as not everyone has a .NET setup available.

I just reproduced this with your MRP and can confirm the behaviour you described. 

I haven't really looked into the CharacterBody2D code in depth myself, but I have a suspicion as to the problem.

When you just move right, and you hit a slope, the engine will move you up that slope, but it will not adjust your velocity.y. So when you move up the slope by walking, your velocity.y remains 0 the whole time. If you stop velocity.x, then everything will stop.

However, when you jump, while still moving right, the steep slope ensures that the land comes up to meet your jump and stops your jump while your velocity is still -ve (up). That is, you are still moving upward when the land races up to stop you. 

As you keep moving right, your velocity.y will remain -ve and you are not applying gravity (because you are on_floor() ). Then when you finally release 'right', you clamp down velocity.x, but you don't do anything about velocity.y (which is still -ve). So effectively, that is when it finishes off the jump and goes straight up in the air (because you have abruptly stopped X velocity, but not Y).

Not sure if this workaround suits: 
```
	# Add the gravity.
	if not is_on_floor():
		velocity += get_gravity() * delta
	else:
		velocity.y = 0.0
```

Another workaround would be just to damp out velocity.x and velocity.y together (rather than clamping them separately).

I am not sure that we want to do anything in the engine about this, or even can. I will leave that to a CharacterBody2D expert.
